newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedes study if mobile phones harm users' health.
newsitem.headline: Swedes study if mobile phones harm users' health.

text.p: The world's widest investigation into the possibly harmful effects of mobile telephones has begun in Norway and Sweden, its team leader said Tuesday.
Some 12,000 people in Sweden, which has one of the world's highest per capita use of mobile phones, and 5,000 Norwegians will take part in the survey, partly funded by the mobile telephone industry.

The project leader, Professor Kjell Hansson Mild of Sweden's National Institute for Working Life, said many users of mobile phones had complained of headaches, a feeling of warmth or tingling in the face and head, dizziness and drowsiness.
Other complaints included nausea, memory loss and lack of concentration, he said by telephone from the institute at Umea, in northern Sweden.
"It is now time that we thoroughly investigate," he said.
Sweden had been chosen because it is a country with one of the highest concentrations of mobile phones, about 2 million.
"We are looking at the heavy users of phones rather than people who make one call per day," Hansson Mild said.
Previous studies, though more narrowly based, have failed to prove any definitive link between the use of mobile phones and ill-health.
